newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks open mixed, miners buoyed by metals.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks open mixed, miners buoyed by metals.

text.p: Australian shares opened mixed on Thursday with industrial issues dragged down by a weake Wall Street but resources buoyed by stronger metal prices and takeover offers for Highlands Gold and Placer Pacific.
At 10.20 a.m. (2320 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 0.5 points lower at 2,376.2.
Market volume was lifted by the inclusion of 33 percent of Highlands stock which was bought by Canadian bidder, Placer Dome, after the close of trade on Wednesday.
Placer Dome also announced it planned to buy the 25 percent of Placer Pacific that it did not already own.
Brokers said the stronger copper price had a lot to do with the market's resilience with bellwether resource issues BHP and MIM finding early support.
"Investors are more confident that what we are seeing now is a sustainable recovery in the price of copper which is very good news for BHP," a dealer from a Melbourne-based brokerage said.
Gold miners with exposure with exposure to Papua New Guinea were well sought after following Placer Dome's move on Highlands with Lihir Gold and Goldfields the key beneficiaries.
At 11.00 a.m. (2400 GMT), Lihir stock was 18 cents higher at A$2.49 (US$2.02) and Goldfields shares were 19 cents up at A$2.65.
Coca-Cola Amatil stock was also firmer, rising 25 cents to A$13.40 by 11.00 a.m. (2400 GMT). Dealers said the company's shares had been oversold earlier this week.
